newsitem.title: USA: SPX Q1 revenues down from divestitures.
newsitem.headline: SPX Q1 revenues down from divestitures.

text.p: SPX Corp on Tuesday reported lower revenues for the first quarter, reflecting the sale of its Sealed Power and Hy-Lift units, as well as $20 million in one-time dealer equipment sales that occurred a year ago.
SPX, which provides specialty service tools, equipment and components to the auto industry, had total revenues of $236.7 million for the period, down from $292.3 million.
Revenues from the firm's Service Solutions unit were $143.8 million, down from $156.6 million. Original Equipment Component sales were $92.9 million, down 32 percent from $135.7 million.

On an operating basis, first quarter earnings rose to $1.68 a share from $0.20. SPX officials said the firm has adopted a new financial strategy that emphasizes "economic value added" or EVA, and reduces costs.
"We remain positive in our outlook for the business in 1997 and beyond," John Blystone, chairman, president and chief executive officer said in a statement.
